name: Thailand
genZNote: Thailand is the only Southeast Asian country never colonised by a European power — it literally means 'Land of the Free' — and it's been running on the same royal-Buddhist cultural backbone for centuries while still being one of the region's biggest tourism and manufacturing hubs.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located in mainland Southeast Asia, bordered by Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, and Malaysia, with coastlines on the Gulf of Thailand and the Andaman Sea.
The fertile Chao Phraya River basin in the central plains is the historic agricultural and population heartland, including the capital Bangkok.
Tropical monsoon climate with mountainous, forested terrain in the north and popular island/beach regions in the south.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Thai is the official language; Theravada Buddhism is practiced by the large majority of the population and deeply shapes daily life, festivals, and architecture (ornate wats/temples).
The monarchy holds deep cultural reverence, and the Thai king is a central, highly respected national symbol.
Famous for its cuisine (balancing sweet, sour, salty, spicy flavours), Muay Thai martial arts, and major festivals like Songkran (Thai New Year water festival).

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system; the King is head of state while an elected Prime Minister and National Assembly govern.
The only Southeast Asian nation never formally colonised by a European power, historically credited to skilful diplomacy between British and French colonial spheres.
Has experienced numerous military coups and periods of military-influenced government through its modern history, alongside periods of democratic governance.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A regional hub for medical tourism, known for high-quality, affordable private healthcare and hospital infrastructure.
Strong agricultural science base supporting its position as one of the world's largest rice exporters.
Growing automotive and electronics manufacturing sector, sometimes called the 'Detroit of Asia' for vehicle assembly.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A founding member of ASEAN and one of Southeast Asia's most tourism-dependent and internationally connected economies.
Maintains close ties with both the United States (a treaty ally) and China, balancing relationships as part of its historical non-aligned diplomatic tradition.
An active participant in regional economic and security groupings across the Indo-Pacific.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Thailand share deep civilisational links through the historic spread of Buddhism and Hindu culture (Thai royal ceremonies still use Brahmin priests and Sanskrit-rooted terms).
Part of India's 'Act East' policy and the BIMSTEC regional grouping alongside other Bay of Bengal nations.
Growing trade, tourism, and connectivity cooperation, including discussions on the India-Myanmar-Thailand trilateral highway.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A major manufacturing and export economy, particularly strong in automobiles, electronics, and agricultural products.
One of the world's largest rice exporters, along with significant exports of rubber, seafood, and processed foods.
Tourism is a major economic pillar, drawing millions of visitors annually to destinations like Bangkok, Phuket, and Chiang Mai.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Never having been colonised by a European power in Southeast Asia.
World-renowned Buddhist temples, cuisine, and tourism destinations.
Being a major global rice exporter and Southeast Asian manufacturing hub.
Muay Thai and a deeply respected constitutional monarchy.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Thai Baht (THB).
A major manufacturing and tourism-driven economy in Southeast Asia, strong in automobiles, electronics, and agriculture (notably rice exports).
Bangkok is a major regional business and tourism hub.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Diverse ecosystems from northern mountains to southern tropical islands and coral reefs.
Faces marine-conservation challenges balancing tourism growth with reef and coastline protection.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: The only Southeast Asian country never colonized by a European power, historically known as Siam.
Renamed Thailand in 1939; has experienced numerous military coups alongside periods of constitutional monarchy governance.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1932 revolution ended absolute monarchy, establishing a constitutional monarchy.
Has had numerous constitutions and military coups since, reflecting recurring tension between military, monarchy, and elected government.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: Geo-Informatics and Space Technology Development Agency (GISTDA) leads national satellite programmes.
A significant regional hub for automotive manufacturing, often called the 'Detroit of Asia'.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Muay Thai (Thai boxing) is the national martial art, practised worldwide.
The historic city of Ayutthaya and Sukhothai are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Buddhist temples (wats) and the Grand Palace in Bangkok are iconic cultural landmarks.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of ASEAN.
Member of the UN and APEC; a close long-standing ally of the United States in Southeast Asia.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Thailand is a Southeast Asian constitutional monarchy, historically never colonised, known for Buddhist culture, tourism, and manufacturing.
keyFacts: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system.
One of the world's largest rice exporters.
Founding ASEAN member; part of India's Act East policy and BIMSTEC.
commonConfusion: Thailand is a constitutional monarchy, not an absolute one — an elected government and parliament run day-to-day affairs.

highYieldFacts: Thailand: only Southeast Asian country never colonised by a European power.
Founding ASEAN member; key BIMSTEC partner for India's Act East policy.
One of the world's top rice exporters; major automobile manufacturing hub.
commonTraps: Assuming Thailand is a republic — it is a constitutional monarchy.
Confusing BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal grouping) with ASEAN membership scope.
mustRemember: Thailand: constitutional monarchy, Buddhist-majority, rice/auto export powerhouse, key BIMSTEC and Act East partner for India.

sources.name: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India — India-Thailand Relations
